conviction_note: The quarter is pinned by the 7 July guide: FY26 sales of $330.5-331.5M less Q1-Q3 ($73.5M + $80.0M + $85.9M = $239.4M) implies Q4 sales of $91.1-92.1M, and consensus is $91.6M. So the print turns on the first FY27 guide. On revenue that guide is at risk: the exit comp is -3 to -4% and FY27 pricing is planned below FY26, against $389M consensus. On margin it leans positive: restaurant-level margin heads toward 20%, the labor gains are holding, and the rewards relaunch and the Yoshi collab started on schedule. Positioning is crowded and de-rated (about 25% of float short, Citi target cut to $36, bearish sentiment up to 35%). These offset, so p_up is 51, barely off the non-result, and abs_move_pct is 13, above the 11.9% median because a first FY guide meets a crowded, thin float. The findings sum to +0.7 against a scaled +0.26. Both are small and share a sign, and the gap is the positive positioning item, which counts in the sum but carries little weight in p_up.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue of $91.6M and EPS of $0.22 (whisper $0.19), from Earnings Whispers 2026-10-28 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KRUS/22325). This sits inside the company's own guide: FY26 sales of $330.5-331.5M (8-K 2026-07-07, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm) less Q1-Q3 implies Q4 of $91.1-92.1M. FY26 consensus revenue is $330.3M (stockanalysis, 9 analysts). The FY27 bar is about $389M revenue and $0.24 EPS (stockanalysis summary, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krus/forecast/). It has one source, so findings that depend on the FY27 bar are capped small.
positioning_check: No listed options, so there is no skew. Short interest is about 1.8M shares and 6.6 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, up from 1.6M and 7.2 days at 2026-09-15 (sweep row; curvedtrading via search; the direct fetch returned 403). Fintel shows 1.72M shares, 24.6% of float, 9.8 days to cover and a 0.31% borrow rate, undated (https://fintel.io/s/us/krus, read 2026-11-05). That is roughly 25% of a 6.7-7.3M float, a crowded short. Spot of $36.47 is 54% below the 52-week high. The stock was about $31.80 on 2026-10-28, near the post-report low of $29.69, and has bounced about 15% into the print (run_up_5d +4.4%, run_up_20d -8.7%). Citi cut its target to $36 from $59 on 2026-10-26 and D.A. Davidson to $55 from $65 on 2026-10-15. Earnings Whispers' bearish reading rose to 35.4% from 21.6%.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 sales are effectively pre-announced. The 7 July FY26 guide of $330.5-331.5M less reported Q1-Q3 sales of $239.4M ($73.5M + $80.0M + $85.9M) implies Q4 of $91.1-92.1M, about +15-16% on Q4 FY25's $79.4M and an implied comp of roughly -3 to -4%. Consensus of $91.6M sits at the midpoint, so the reported top line should land on the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 FY26 (2026-07-07) sales of $85.9M missed the $86.27M consensus slightly and the guide was narrowed down, and the stock moved +0.79%. Q2 FY26 (2026-04-07) delivered +8.6% comps and the stock fell -17.78%. Reported-quarter sales have not set the sign on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The guide gave Q4 to within $1M after two of its three months had elapsed, and consensus of $91.6M sits at the midpoint. This is filed so the judges can see that the quarter's top line is not where the move comes from.
findings.independence: Consensus of $91.6M and EPS of $0.22 come from Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KRUS/22325, 2026-10-28). Q1 and Q2 sales come from the company's 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1772177/000119312526006345/krus-ex99_1.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1772177/000119312526145572/krus-ex99_1.htm).

findings.finding: On the Q3 call, management said Kura is receiving refunds on tariffs it paid on 'other cost items' where it was the importer of record, and confirmed this is a one-time Q4 tailwind. Q4 cost of goods and EPS can therefore print better than the FY26 run-rate of about 30% COGS and 18.5% restaurant-level margin implies, against an EPS bar of $0.22 (whisper $0.19). The amount was not quantified.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a tariff refund. Margin beats on this name have bought little: the Q3 FY26 margin beat and raised margin guide gave +0.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed on the call but never quantified. If analysts had modelled it, the EPS whisper would sit above consensus rather than at $0.19, below $0.22. It is one-time and the food-ingredient tariffs are not included, so it has no path into the FY27 guide.
findings.independence: The background is the CIT order of IEEPA refunds and CBP's refund portal opening in April 2026 (https://grantthornton.com/insights/newsletters/tax/2026/hot-topics/apr-28/ieepa-refunds-begin-lawsuit-against-new-tariffs-proceeds). That is general and says nothing specific to the company.

findings.finding: The FY27 revenue guide is at risk against the roughly $389M (+17.8%) consensus. The exit comp is about -3 to -4% (Q4 implied by the guide; Q3 traffic was -5.1%). Management said FY27 pricing will be 'below where we came in for fiscal 2026', and cannibalization should persist into 1H FY27. That leaves unit growth above 20% to carry the whole revenue line, against a FY26 base of $331M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last first-FY-guide print (2025-11-06, FY26 guide of $330-334M against $338.5M consensus per TheFly) moved -11.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Citi's target cut to $36 on 2026-10-26 and the 35% bearish reading suggest estimates were trimmed, but the visible FY27 consensus still reads +17.8% revenue growth, which roughly assumes flat comps. If the market had fully priced a negative-comp FY27, consensus would sit near unit growth less a comp drag, around $375-380M.
findings.independence: The FY27 consensus figure is from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krus/forecast/ (one source). The analyst's implied Q4 comp of -3 to -4% also appears in Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KRUS/22325). Both rest partly on the same Q3 call.

findings.finding: Margins should lead the FY27 guide. Management said FY27 restaurant-level margin will get 'a lot closer to that 20% historical goal a lot faster', against 18.5% guided for FY26 (raised in July). The supporting levers are about 200bp of FY26 labor improvement, Bikkura Pon voucher changes worth up to 50bp (update promised for November), in-house preventive maintenance and vendor renegotiations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 raised the margin guide to about 18.5% while comps were -0.4%, and the stock moved +0.79%. Margin has not been the line this stock trades on; traffic and comps have.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY27 EPS consensus of $0.24 against a FY26 of -$0.05 already assumes leverage, so a margin guide near 19.5-20% is partly expected. What is not visible is the November Bikkura Pon update and its size.
findings.independence: The Q3 8-K shows labor at 30.6% of sales against 33.1% a year earlier and restaurant-level margin at 19.1% against 18.2% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm). It is the same company and partly the same event.

findings.finding: The tariff regime on Japanese imports changed inside Q4. Section 122's 10% surcharge lapsed on 24 July 2026 and Section 301 duties took over, with a 12.5% combined floor for Japan. Q3's 200bp tariff COGS headwind was incurred under the 10% regime, so the FY27 COGS run-rate on imported ingredients is slightly worse than Q3's, not better.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff-driven COGS (+200bp) accompanied the Q3 FY26 print, which moved +0.79%. Tariffs have not set the sign here.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. Food-item exemptions and how the costs pass through vendors are unknown, and FY27 against the FY26 average (about 15% under IEEPA in H1, 10% after) is roughly flat. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: The 301 rate is also reported at https://www.dorsey.com/newsresources/publications/client-alerts/2026/7/announced-section-301-tariffs. This is a proxy with no company confirmation.

findings.finding: Both FY27 Q1 traffic levers launched on schedule. The tiered rewards relaunch (Yellowfin/Bigeye/Bluefin tiers, new app) went live around 2026-10-06. The Yoshi Bikkura Pon collaboration starts 2026-11-01, with the larger promotions from 11-04. Management sized Yoshi as comparable to Kirby, a mid-single-digit comp lift, and a $85-spend gate on the blanket promotion supports mix. That gives the call quarter-to-date and holiday-quarter material to talk to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY26 print (2026-01-07), with comps of -2.5% but forward commentary of improving traffic and collabs, moved +16.7%. Forward comp commentary has been the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Both launches are public, but no one has quantified a Q1 FY27 comp. If they were priced as a recovery, the stock would not be sitting at the Citi target of $36, about 5% above where it was on 10-28 near its low.
findings.independence: Yoshi start dates are from Siliconera (https://www.siliconera.com/next-kura-sushi-event-involves-yoshi-and-the-mysterious-book/). The Kirby-comparable claim is from the Q3 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1881185-20260708).

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded and de-rated into the print. About 25% of float is short, with 6.6-9.8 days to cover. Two pre-print target cuts (Citi to $36 from $59 on 10-26; D.A. Davidson to $55 from $65 on 10-15) lowered the bar. Earnings Whispers' bearish reading rose to 35.4% from 21.6%. The stock sits 54% below its 52-week high, although it has already bounced about 15% from $31.80 on 10-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest moves in the history are up: +31.62% (2025-04-08) and +16.7% (2026-01-07), both on prints that relieved a weak-traffic narrative. The baseline shows 3 of 7 prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: A crowded short is the market's statement, not something it missed. It is filed because it skews the reaction to any relief upward. The 15% bounce since 10-28 shows some covering has already happened, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Short interest comes from the sweep row (FINRA via curvedtrading, 2026-09-30 settlement) and Fintel (https://fintel.io/s/us/krus). Sentiment and the price on 10-28 are from https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KRUS/22325.

findings.finding: Unit openings caught up after the Q3 delays. The 15 October results notice counts 96 restaurants, against 94 at the 7 July release, consistent with the FY26 target of 16 being met. Management said the FY27 pipeline is 'higher than 20%' unit growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 FY26 opening delays (about six revenue months lost) were disclosed with a narrowed sales guide, and the stock moved +0.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: The count sits in boilerplate that nobody aggregates, but it only confirms the guided 16. Its value is that the FY27 unit guide starts from a full FY26 class with no slip.
findings.independence: Q3 release counts 91 at May 31 plus 3 after (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm).

findings.finding: Gas prices, which management blamed for Q3 frequency loss, fell from the AAA national average peak of $4.564 (2026-05-21) to under $4.00 by mid-June, then sat near $4.06-4.10 through August, a record August. Management said on 7 July it was 'beginning to see a little bit of benefit' in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26's -5.1% traffic, attributed to gas prices, came with a +0.79% move.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside the Q4 guide set on 7 July, so it bears mainly on the traffic commentary rather than the number. It is a macro proxy.
findings.independence: The June drop below $4 is also reported at https://wtop.com/news/2026/06/us-gasoline-prices-fall-below-4-on-average-for-the-first-time-since-march/. The Q4 benefit comment is from the Q3 call. This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Peers have reported since Kura last spoke, and the read is mixed to soft. Chipotle (10-28) reported +0.8% transactions but described an industry slowdown early in October before traffic returned. Cava (11-04) cut its FY same-restaurant sales guide to 3-4% from 4-6% and fell about 10% after hours. Kura's September-October quarter-to-date commentary falls in that window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company record of trading on peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Cava's cut came after the close on 11-04, one session before this print, so it may not yet be reflected in KRUS. Chipotle's read was positive overall. The net is small.
findings.independence: Cava's release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639438/000162828026070159/earningsrelease2026q3.htm. These are proxies, not counterparties.

findings.finding: Liquidity is drawing down to fund openings. Cash fell to $24.4M at 2026-05-31 from $47.5M at 2025-08-31, plus $19.9M of short-term and $21.8M of long-term investments. Capex runs about $2.5M a unit, and FY27 needs 19 or more units. The company has used a follow-on offering before (800k shares, $64.4M, in the FY25 comparative period).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for an offering announced at a print.
findings.why_not_priced: No financing has been announced. Any money raised would fund a corroborated unit pipeline (96 units, more than 20% growth), so under the financing rule the sign is near zero. A raise near the lows would be dilutive, which leaves a slight negative tail.
findings.independence: Capex of about $2.5M a unit is from the Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm). The finding rests on the same company documents.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The evidence is balanced: a soft FY27 revenue setup against a margin story and crowded, de-rated positioning. That fits a stock 54% off its high that has already bounced 15% in a week, so neither side is clearly unpriced and p_up sits at 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the tariff refund has no path to the FY27 guide, so it was cut from +0.5 to +0.2.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): FY27 revenue risk cut from -1.5 to -1.2 and the Section 301 tariff from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money would fund a corroborated pipeline of 96 units and more than 20% growth, so the liquidity finding went from -0.3 to -0.1.
Lesson 1 (this name has not paid for margin beats; Q3's margin raise bought +0.79%): margin path cut from +1.0 to +0.7 and the rewards/Yoshi launch from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson 5 (proxies stay small): the peer read was cut from -0.5 to -0.2 because Chipotle's read was mixed. The gas finding stays at +0.2.
The positioning finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.5 because the 15% bounce since 10-28 shows covering has already started; p_up moved from 52 to 51.
Lesson 6: the bar was confirmed against the company guide plus Earnings Whispers, so the reported-quarter finding stays at 0. The FY27 bar has one source, so the guidance findings stay capped small.
